n: Sanrio Puroland (サンリオピューロランド)
address: Tama Center (Tama New Town), Tama, Tokyo — by Tama-Center Station (Keiō / Odakyū / Tama Monorail)
w: Indoor theme park opened in 1990 in Tama New Town, half an hour from Shinjuku: a Hello Kitty musical, Kitty's house, live shows and meet-and-greets with My Melody, Cinnamoroll, Gudetama and Aggretsuko.
anime: Hello Kitty & the Sanrio universe — the company's own indoor park ('Hello Kitty Land')

n: Kamakurakōkōmae Railway Crossing — Slam Dunk (鎌倉高校前 踏切)
address: By Kamakurakōkōmae Station (Enoden line), Koshigoe, Kamakura, Kanagawa
w: The seaside Enoden level crossing just east of Kamakurakōkōmae Station, with the Pacific behind the passing tram — immortalised in the Slam Dunk opening and one of Japan's most-visited anime pilgrimage spots.
anime: Slam Dunk — the railroad crossing from the anime's opening sequence
gs: Wikipedia Kamakurakōkōmae Station infobox (35°18′24″N 139°30′02″E) — the crossing is on the station's east side

n: Animate Ikebukuro Flagship Store (アニメイト池袋本店)
w: Animate's flagship since 1983, expanded into ten floors of shops, event spaces, cafés and a theatre — recognised by Guinness World Records as the world's largest anime store, anchoring Ikebukuro's otaku quarter.
anime: All franchises — Guinness-certified largest anime store, the hub of Ikebukuro's Otome Road scene
